paper_title: THE CROSS-SECTION OF VOLATILITY AND EXPECTED RETURNS
summary: Deprioritize. The strategy comes from Ang, Hodrick, Xing and Zhang (2004), who sort stocks each month on idiosyncratic volatility relative to the Fama-French three-factor model and find that the lowest-volatility quintile outperforms the highest. We tested the long-only, equal-weighted lowest-volatility quintile on a 415-name S&P 500 survivor universe over 2015 to 2025 and found net CAGR of 11.92% against 12.71% for the equal-weight universe, with Sharpe 0.63 against 0.65. The Monte Carlo fund simulation put the probability of positive NPV at 34%, with a median incremental fee PV of -$600k against the equal-weight universe fund. The edge fails at 10 bps, holds in neither sub-period, and the group ranking runs the wrong way, so the recommendation is to deprioritize even though implementation reliability is green.
